notes: The distributive ish ish is split one word to one morpheme, since the ASV writes two words (every one) and rule 30's one-English-word condition is unmet, so rule 2 splits it. The competing readings — fusion, or a single rendered occurrence beside an unrepresented one — are recorded in the units.
Both coordinating waws are rendered or and take that word (rule 14).
The closing verbless clause puts shall be on the preposition, headed on upon (rule 49).
